I'm 69 this year, been farming this land since I was a young girl — that's over 50 years now. My father taught me, and his father taught him. I never went to school, can't read the characters on the fertilizer bags, but I know this land. I got 12 mu in Quzhou, Hebei. Seven people under my roof, though my son and his wife work in the factory in the city and send some money back when they can. My daughter-in-law helps on the farm when she's not looking after the grandchildren.

For the wheat, I planted it last fall around the tenth of October, same as always. I bought the seed from Old Wang's shop — the same kind my neighbor Li uses, the one that did well for him two years ago. I already put down the base fertilizer before winter: about one big bag of that compound fertilizer and half a bag of urea for each mu. Now it's spring and the wheat is greening up. I'll topdress another half bag of urea per mu when the wheat starts jointing, maybe around Qingming time. If I don't, the wheat turns yellow and the heads get small — I learned that the hard way in the drought year. I'll irrigate three times total: once before winter (already done), once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Water costs money now, they put meters on the wells, but dry wheat means no crop. Last year I got about 380 jin per mu. This year looks about the same.

The cotton is on 4 mu, the south plot where the soil is sandier. I plant around the twentieth of April, after the last cold spell. Cotton needs picking over and over, and at my age it's hard on my back, but my daughter-in-law helps and my sister's family comes for the first picking. I use less fertilizer on cotton than wheat — about one bag of compound for every two mu, and a sprinkle of urea when the buds come. Two irrigations, and I watch for the bollworms. If I see them, I spray. I don't put more pesticide than I need, it costs too much.

For maize, I plant right after we cut the wheat — no time to waste, usually around June 12th or 15th. The window is tight, less than a week sometimes. I hire the tractor man to rotary till after harvest, then we plant. I buy hybrid seed every year from the shop, you can't save maize seed, everyone knows that. One good dose of compound fertilizer at planting, and if July is dry I'll irrigate once or twice. Maize is easier than cotton, thank goodness.

Money is always tight. The fertilizer prices went up again, so I'm not putting more than last year. My neighbor Zhang tried cutting back on fertilizer and his wheat was thin like straw, so I'm not taking that risk. I'd rather spend a bit more and make sure we have grain to eat and cotton to sell. The family needs cash for the grandchildren's school fees in September, so I can't spend everything on inputs. I do what I did last year, with small changes if I saw something work for my neighbors.
